claim: Diagnostic failures cannot replace the existing guard error
scope: new failing-guard diagnostic event plus unchanged receipt writer and baseline teardown
premises: the original peer-binding guard condition is true
receipt writer is functioning before the new diagnostic event
no independent out-of-band terminal record preserves the saved guard error

steps.fact: The guard records baseline-original-peer-binding-mismatch before constructing/throwing its original error.
recorder.event pushes the record and synchronously calls its sink.
A sink write failure latches failed=true and firstError=transportFault; future emits throw firstError.
recordPeerDiagnostic catches this direct sink exception and best-effort logs the diagnostic fault; then returns.
The same original guard error is thrown and captured as failure by the surrounding main catch.
If fixture.cleanup emits, its failed sink throws; cleanup catch attempts completion-secondary-cleanup-error through the same failed writer and escapes with transportFault.
Even if cleanup emits nothing and returns, unconditional worker-cleaned emission throws the latched transportFault before the saved guard is rethrown.
recordWorkerError preserves its incoming error, which can now be transportFault; it cannot recover a saved guard that never reaches it.

inference: Local capture exceptions are suppressed. Unconditional end-to-end original-error preservation is unsupported; a source-supported masking path exists.
requiredNarrowCorrection: Qualify report, freeze and comment to state the local helper guarantee only; receipt-sink failures remain operational faults under unchanged transport/teardown, with no unconditional primary-error preservation credit.
reason: The local helper cannot control later unconditional or secondary-cleanup emissions. Logging original context may retain an extra fact but does not establish terminal error ordering or release.
nextEnforcementWitness: If end-to-end failure preservation is later claimed, separately bind/admit a controlled writer failure at this diagnostic event, retain guard and transport/cleanup faults distinctly, and verify teardown. No such run is admitted here.
